facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks

concepts.why: The patient presented with amenorrhea and a high serum hCG level, and ultrasonography confirmed a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks.
The patient presented with abdominal pain and a tender midline abdominal mass, which are consistent with complications of an intrauterine pregnancy.
The patient had a history of thyroid condition, undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone, and was prescribed methimazole, which are consistent with hyperthyroidism.
The patient presented with constipation, which is a symptom that can be related to various gastrointestinal conditions.
The patient's constipation may be related to her pregnancy, as hormonal changes during pregnancy can cause constipation.
The patient presented with a tender midline abdominal mass, which was later confirmed to be a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks.
The patient's history of thyroid condition, undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone, and prescription of methimazole may indicate a risk of thyroid storm.
The patient's pregnancy may be contributing to her hyperthyroidism, as hormonal changes during pregnancy can affect thyroid function.
It explains the initially negative point-of-care urine human chorionic gonadotropin test in the context of a confirmed pregnancy.
